title: Pakistan Kills 21 TTP Militants in Multiple Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Operations; Revises North Waziristan Infiltration Toll to 25
detail: Pakistan's military said security forces killed 21 Fitna al-Khawarij (TTP) militants in multiple engagements across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa between September 3 and 5, 2026. ISPR said 10 militants were killed in a fresh clash in North Waziristan and 7 more in a separate North Waziristan engagement, while joint operations in Kohat and Dera Ismail Khan districts killed 4. Clearance operations were continuing. Separately, ISPR revised upward the toll from the August 31-September 1 North Waziristan cross-border infiltration attempt, saying the number of militants 'trying to infiltrate and effectively neutralised' had risen to 25, up from the 15 initially reported. ISPR said the repeated border incidents 'vindicated' Pakistan's position that the Afghan Taliban had failed to deny the use of Afghan soil to militant groups.

title: Taliban Detains Three Prominent Shia Leaders Tied to Khatam al-Nabieen Seminary Dispute
detail: On Sunday, September 6, 2026, Taliban authorities detained three prominent Shia figures connected to the Khatam al-Nabieen seminary dispute: Sayed Mohammad Hossein 'Sufi' Gardizi, who headed the complex's public relations office; Sayed Hassan Sharifi Balkhabi; and Mohammad Hossein Sangardoost. Five additional staff from the public relations office — including a cook and two guards — were also detained. The office, which represented Hazara and Shia elders and operated out of a property in Kabul's Sarkariz area linked to former political leader Mohammad Mohaqiq, was closed. The Islamic Unity Party of Afghanistan (Hezb-e-Wahdat) said the detentions came as roughly 50-60 Shia scholars had planned a meeting to discuss the fate of those already held at the seminary and seek their release. The Taliban government has not publicly commented on the detentions.
